payload.rationale: No current data was supplied, so this is a judgment estimate. The event requires Freddie Mac's PMMS 30-year rate published Thursday Sep 24, 2026 to exceed 7.01%. Based on background knowledge, the PMMS rate spent 2025 mostly between roughly 6.2% and 7.0%, trending down into the low-to-mid 6% range in late 2025 as the Fed eased. Absent knowledge of 2026 developments, the most plausible prior for September 2026 is a rate somewhere in the low-to-high 6% range, making a print above 7.01% less likely than not. Week-to-week PMMS moves are typically small (a few to ~15 bp), so the outcome is dominated by the unknown level in mid-September 2026 rather than one week's volatility. The existence of a 7.01% strike suggests the market maker considered it within a plausible ladder, so rates may be closer to 7% than my late-2025 prior implies; I shift upward for that. Reasons the estimate could be too high: if rates continued easing through 2026 (further Fed cuts, lower term premium), 7.01% would be far out of reach and the true probability near zero. Reasons it could be too low: if inflation or fiscal/term-premium pressures pushed 10-year yields higher in 2026 (as in late 2023 when PMMS exceeded 7.5%), rates could already be at or above 7%, in which case a print above 7.01% would be a near coin flip or better. Given the roughly symmetric ignorance about 2026 and a mildly favorable prior toward sub-7% levels, I estimate about 30%.
limitations: No current or recent PMMS observations supplied; estimate relies on pre-2026 background knowledge only.
Unknown 2026 macro path (Fed policy, inflation, Treasury yields) dominates the outcome.
Cannot observe daily mortgage rate trackers for the Sep 17-23 measurement window.
Contract strike placement was used only as weak contextual inference, not as market odds.
